title: glottogenera: genera defined by a divergence threshold on a language tree, with a release for Glottolog 5.3
description: Genera defined by an explicit rule: on a rooted language tree, a genus is the largest clade whose divergence does not exceed a threshold delta. The rule applies to any tree (an expert classification, or one estimated from data by neighbour-joining, UPGMA or Bayesian inference) and any divergence (a distance between languages averaged over pairs on different branches, or a quantity of the clade such as its age); the package's glottogenera.tree module implements it. The release instantiates it for the 7,674 in-scope languages of Glottolog 5.3, with divergence measured by PMI alignment over the 40-concept ASJP wordlists and delta calibrated against the WALS genera averaged over language families: 1,190 genera, each a complete Glottolog clade, with crown divergence, margins and bootstrap stability. Includes the released tables (also as a CLDF StructureDataset), the full pipeline (Python package with CLI), the vendored Glottolog dump and a web explorer (https://glottogenera.tresoldi.org). Also includes the expert cognate judgements of sixteen published datasets on the 40 ASJP core concepts, used to select the word distance (research/divergence/cognates/). The data are under CC BY 4.0 and the code under the MIT license, except the cognate judgements, which keep the licences of their sources (fourteen CC BY 4.0, one CC BY-NC 4.0, one stating none; see research/divergence/cognates/README.md).
